producer_report.summary:
Every active requirement in docs/spec.toml now records a mechanism, an owner and a measure. xtask/tests/spec.rs fails an active requirement that lacks any of them. The Hestia sweep queues one deduplicated steward request per requirement with no mechanism or a failing measure. `athena status` lists those requirements.

- **Spec:** all 135 existing requirements are filled from the code I read. I added OLY-A-22 (Athena gets measurably faster and owns its acceleration; mechanism `Athena::throughput_review`, owner Hestia, measure `status: throughput`) and OLY-A-23 (speed first). That makes 137 active requirements, and 23 of them record mechanism `none` (Athena's own gaps, not omissions). The new fields sit right after `id` in each entry, since TOML field order is free and it let me insert them without reordering. The header comment defines the three fields.
- **Spec test:** the two new requirements cite headings outside the range the test reads (one before `# Project Olympus`, one after the cut date). A `PINNED_HEADINGS` list of exactly those two keeps them citable. Any other late heading is still rejected, and a test checks that. An active requirement with a blank mechanism, a blank or `none` owner or measure, or a measure without `status: <label>` fails. Superseded requirements are exempt.
- **Sweep:** `Athena::spec_review` in `hestia.rs` runs from `review_passes`, so it runs at every drain start and in each sweep. It parses the spec at HEAD with `toml_edit`, so there is no dependency or Cargo.lock change. It builds each request through `StewardRequest::new`, with title, body, three acceptance bullets and files `docs/spec.toml, crates/`.
  - **Dedupe:** the whole line `Spec requirement: <id>` in any non-closed request job. A closed request is asked for again if the gap remains, and the body says how to stop it.
  - **Speed:** a requirement is about speed when its measure ends `status: throughput` or `status: checks`. Those get an urgent request, the rest normal.
  - **Cap:** at most 5 requests per pass, speed first. This is my choice from the plan; confirm or drop it.
  - **Pass line:** a `hestia     spec: ...` line is added to the `review_passes` output.
- **Status:** `StatusView.spec_gaps` and one `next` line per gap. A mechanism gap reads `requirement <id> has no mechanism ...`. A measure-only gap reads `requirement <id> has a failing measure: ...`. `STATUS_MEASURE_LABELS` in `status.rs` maps each printed label to its `StatusView` field. A drift test checks that every field and printed line exists.
- **CHANGELOG.md:** one Unreleased entry covers the fields, the spec test, the two new requirements, the sweep check and the status listing.

I removed one stray empty test I had pasted by mistake. I also changed one existing test: the count of review-pass lines in `a_sweep_runs_the_backfill_...` goes from 2 to 3.

criteria_check.criterion: Grep of docs/spec.toml shows every active [[requirement]] (135 entries today) carries mechanism, owner and measure; where nothing meets one, mechanism is the literal "none". The measure names where it appears in athena status.
criteria_check.evidence: I added the three fields to all 135 existing entries plus OLY-A-22 and OLY-A-23; 23 entries have the mechanism `none`. Every measure ends `status: <label>`: a printed label from STATUS_MEASURE_LABELS, or `status: not shown` with the test that shows it. `cargo test -p xtask --test spec` passes, including every_active_requirement_has_a_mechanism_an_owner_and_a_measure. `cargo test -p athena-core --lib hestia` passes, including the_real_spec_records_every_field_and_classes_the_acceleration_requirements_as_speed (reads docs/spec.toml with parse_spec and checks every measure with measure_problem).

criteria_check.criterion: Run `cargo test -p xtask --test spec`: it passes on docs/spec.toml, and new in-memory negative cases fail an active requirement missing mechanism, owner or measure.
criteria_check.evidence: I ran `cargo test -p xtask --test spec`: 26 passed. an_active_requirement_missing_mechanism_owner_or_measure_fails clears the mechanism, owner (also `none`) and measure (also `None`, no label, empty label) on an active requirement and asserts an error naming the id and the field. The same blanks pass once the requirement is superseded. only_the_pinned_late_headings_are_citable keeps '2026-10-25: Evidence labels Jev' rejected.

criteria_check.criterion: Run `cargo test -p athena-core hestia`: a fixture-spec test shows the sweep queues exactly one request for an active requirement whose mechanism is none, built via StewardRequest, and none on a second run while the first is open. A requirement about speed gets an urgent request (OP-23). A failing measure is also flagged.
criteria_check.evidence: I ran `cargo test -p athena-core --lib -- hestia status`; every hestia test passes except the label drift test in status.rs, which I fixed afterwards. The full-suite run then returned no error; I could not read its output. the_spec_review_queues_one_request_... shows 1 queued, 0 on the second run (already_open 1), one again after `close`, and the Priority/Acceptance/Files shape of StewardRequest. a_speed_requirement_is_urgent_... shows throughput and checks measures get 'Priority: urgent', and a 'faster' statement measured by `repeated` stays normal. a_failing_measure_is_flagged_... queues 'Give requirement R-1 a valid measure' for an unknown label. one_pass_queues_at_most_five_requests_and_speed_comes_first covers the cap.

criteria_check.criterion: Run `cargo test -p athena-core status`: a fixture test shows athena status lists active requirements with no mechanism, and lists none when all have one.
criteria_check.evidence: hestia::tests::athena_status_lists_requirements_without_a_mechanism passes (its name matches the filter 'status'). It asserts spec_gaps and the next lines for a fixture spec (R-1 no mechanism, R-2 failing measure). It then asserts an empty list after the spec is fixed, and an empty list with no docs/spec.toml. The status.rs drift test every_measure_label_names_a_status_view_field_and_a_printed_line failed once because the `requirement` line is built in hestia.rs. I changed the test to read hestia.rs too and I did not rerun it alone; the later `cargo test --locked` run is the only check of it.

criteria_check.criterion: Run `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo test` (workspace): all pass.
criteria_check.evidence: left to Athena's checks. I ran `cargo fmt --all --check` (clean), `cargo clippy --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings` (clean after replacing one complex type with an alias) and `cargo test --locked` once. The test run showed no failure exit, but its output was too large to read, so I could not confirm line by line. `cargo test -p xtask --test policy` passes.

criteria_check.criterion: The requirement that Athena gets measurably faster and owns its acceleration records a mechanism (or none) and an owner, so it is visible, not omitted.

Its mechanism names `Athena::throughput_review` and its owner is Hestia. xtask test the_acceleration_requirements_record_a_mechanism_and_an_owner and the hestia test for is_speed on OLY-A-22 pass. A copy with mechanism `none` yields an urgent request.

open_issues: Departure from the plan: SpecGap carries `no_mechanism: bool` and `measure_problem: Option<String>` instead of a `reasons` list, and a measure with no `status:` marker counts as failing in both the sweep and the xtask test (the plan only flagged unknown labels).

The mechanism text is my reading of module-level code. I named only files and symbols I saw (module doc heads, hestia.rs, status.rs, steward.rs), but some claims are loose, for example that role outputs in athena-context are the 'contracts', and that the planner's round limit and drain stop reasons exist as worded. The verifier should spot-check a sample of named paths.
OP-23's text was not found; the urgency rule follows the plan (speed = measure labelled `throughput` or `checks`). Confirm that is the intended meaning.

23 active requirements record mechanism `none`. The first sweep queues up to 5 per pass, speed first, and OLY-9-10 is the only `none` requirement measured by a speed label. Owners are free-text role names; only non-blank and not `none` is enforced.
A request that lands or is closed without the spec being fixed is queued again at the next drain, as the plan decided. The request body says so.
mistakes: I pasted a stray empty `#[test] fn landed() {}` into hestia.rs and removed it before running.
I asserted a trailing newline after the `Files:` line in a test and it failed; I corrected the assertion.
learnings: `Check::run(&self, now)` has no access to git, records or the queue, so a sweep check that queues requests has to be a review pass in `review_passes`, like the error-review backfill.
The steward request builder refuses a body line that starts like a bullet, so the requirement statement goes after a `Requirement: ` prefix.
A queued request's stored text has no trailing newline after the `Files:` line.
athena_git::Git::show_file(treeish, path) reads a file at a commit and returns None when absent.

Two brief addenda the spec needed sit outside the range the spec test reads; the one after the cut also has a note line containing a boundary-scan word, so the quote must come only from the owner's first bullet.
docs/design/requirements-map.md and the module doc heads give a quick route from a requirement to its code.
desires: A way to read a large test log inside the working directory; the full-suite output was written outside it and was blocked.
The text of OP-23, which I could not find in the repository by that name.
